We need to find templates to break bonds. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find retrosynthetic templates for target molecule. Let's first get functional groups list? Might not need.

We need to propose route manually maybe using known reactions: target is a sulfonamide attached to phenyl, with a conjugated amide attached to an anilide.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: p-tolyl sulfonamide linking to phenyl bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall could be assembled via sulfonyl chloride coupling and amide formation.

Potential retrosynthesis: Disconnection 1: Break sulfonamide S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. So precursor 1: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) attached to phenyl? Actually sulfonyl group attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc...). So we need 4-(methyl) phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl ring, and the other side is attached to an aniline (the tolyl ring). So we could have sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-(methyl) phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl ring at position? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The other side is N attached to tolyl ring (Cc1ccc(N... )cc1). So we could form sulfonamide by reacting 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) with 4-(phenyl) sulfonyl chloride (4-phenylsulfonyl chloride). That sulfonyl chloride could be commercially available? Possibly 4-(phenyl)sulfonyl chloride (also called phenylsulfonyl chloride) is common. But we need phenyl ring with para substituent? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring that also has the conjugated amide side chain. So we need a sulfonyl chloride that is para-substituted with the side chain (C=C-C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). That side chain is not present in commercial sulfonyl chloride. So maybe better to form the side chain first, then sulfonylate.

Alternative: Disconnection at the C=C double bond (retro-aldol) to give aldehyde and amide? The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 attached to phenyl ring. Could be formed via Heck coupling of an aryl bromide with an acrylamide. So precursor: aryl bromide (the phenyl ring with sulfonamide) and acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). That could be made from aniline and acryloyl chloride.

Thus route: Step1: Form sulfonamide between p-toluidine and 4-bromo phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait we need aryl bromide for Heck later. So we could have sulfonyl chloride on a bromophenyl (bromo at para position to sulfonyl). Then after sulfonamide formation, we have aryl bromide attached to sulfonamide, then Heck coupling with acrylamide to install side chain.

Thus precursors: 4-bromo benzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and p-toluidine (commercial). Reaction: sulfonamide formation (nucleophilic substitution). Then Heck coupling with acryloyl anilide (acrylamide with aniline). The acryloyl anilide could be made from acryloyl chloride + 2-aminobiphenyl? Actually the amide is C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (anilide with free NH2). That's N-phenyl-2-aminobenzamide? Wait structure: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. So amide attached to aniline that also has an NH2 ortho? Actually it's N attached to phenyl which also has an NH2 at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an extra NH? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the phenyl (as amide) and the phenyl also has an NH2 substituent at position? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That's an aniline with an amino group at the other end? So it's 1,4-diaminobenzene? Actually the first N is the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl, then the phenyl has an N at the other end (aniline). So it's 4-aminophenyl amide.

Thus the amide is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Wait the side chain is C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 where the phenyl has an NH2 para to the amide. So we need acryloyl chloride + 4-aminophenylamine? Actually we need to form amide between acryloyl and 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine). That yields N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide, which matches.

Thus precursor: p-phenylenediamine (commercial) and acryloyl chloride (commercial) to make the acryloyl anilide.

Thus overall route:

Step1: Synthesize acryloyl anilide: React p-phenylenediamine with acryloyl chloride to give N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide (one amine acylated, other free). This is a standard acylation.

Step2: Form sulfonamide: React p-toluidine with 4-bromo benzenesulfonyl chloride to give p-tolyl sulfonamide attached to 4-bromo phenyl (the aryl bromide). This yields intermediate A.

Step3: Heck coupling between intermediate A (aryl bromide sulfonamide) and acryloyl anilide (as alkene) to give final product.

All precursors: p-toluidine, 4-bromo benzenesulfonyl chloride, p-phenylenediamine, acryloyl chloride. All commercially available and cheap (<$100 each). Total price well under $9999.

Now need to produce JSON route with up to 3 steps. The root is target molecule. Then reaction step 1 (maybe last step first). Typically retrosynthesis tree goes from target to precursors. So root target, child reaction (template for Heck), children: intermediate A (sulfonamide aryl bromide) and acryloyl anilide. Then each intermediate may have its own reaction nodes.

Thus we need template IDs for these reactions. We need to search for templates. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for Heck coupling: functional_groups_broken? The forward reaction forms C-C bond between aryl bromide and alkene, breaks C-Br bond, forms C-C. So functional_groups_broken: "aryl bromide"? Not sure list.
